title: Boron — curated atomic gas supplement, 2026-10-06
body:
# Boron — curated atomic gas supplement, 2026-10-06

Stage status: IMPLEMENTED. Actual terminal verification is recorded in the linked batch receipt. Full MAT scientific and standalone-image acceptance remains PARTIAL.

## Existing owners and reconciliation

MAT:0005 remains Boron. The [unchanged master](../../records/0005-Boron-B/data/structured/0005-Boron-B.yaml) declares neutral MAT:0005:ATOM:B at /atomic_states/0. Existing solid allotropes, isotope and nuclear owners, γ-B28 B2 pairs, B12 motifs, compound and application records retain their separate contexts. The [table manifest](../../records/0005-Boron-B/data/structured/0005-Boron-B-Table-Manifest.yaml) retains eight authored entries and the [graph manifest](../../records/0005-Boron-B/data/structured/0005-Boron-B-Graph-Manifest.yaml) retains ten reservations. Reviewed table 010/graph 011 are added without renumbering or replacing those entries. Original bytes and complete authored prefixes are preserved.

## Primary source and bounded acceptance

The [NIST gas-only page](https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7440428&Units=SI&Mask=1) identifies neutral B, CAS 7440-42-8, InChI=1S/B. One Chase (1998) GAS fit covers **4137.895–6000 K**, on **mol B** basis, with June 1983 review comment. **SRC-000512** is a dated gas retrieval linked through same_work_as to the existing Boron WebBook work **SRC-000064** in the [registry](../../data/registries/sources.yaml). Its original electron-affinity/ion-energetics node remains byte-identical. This is not independent corroboration. The [main snapshot](../../data/catalog/sources/nist-thermochemistry-0005-2026-10-06.html.txt) and [publisher snapshot](../../data/catalog/sources/nist-thermochemistry-0005-2026-10-06-table.html.txt) retain exact bytes and SHA-256 hashes. The [publisher table](https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7440428&Units=SI&Mask=1&Type=JANAFG&Table=on) supplies 20 rows/60 rounded Cp, entropy and enthalpy checks; all passed. All 101 accepted samples are finite and positive; numerical derivatives passed.

The first publisher temperature is printed as 4138., within the fit. The nominal enthalpy increment 79.8453449466 kJ/mol misses printed 79.84 at its half-last-digit tolerance. The exact source minimum 4137.895 K lies within printed cell 4137.5–4138.5 K and uniquely matches all three quantities. The [evaluation index](../../data/catalog/thermochemistry-evaluation-index.json) preserves the raw row and explicit calculation_temperature_K resolution; the accepted CSV starts at 4137.895 K. No tolerance or fit-validity change is made. Ordinary within-range evaluation at 4138 K remains valid; the resolution concerns the publisher row, not a new physical uncertainty.

H(T)-H(298.15 K) retains its published reference offset; it does not authorize evaluating this high-temperature gas fit at 298.15 K or construct a phase-transition path. A separately retained [condensed-phase page](https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7440428&Units=SI&Mask=2) contains one liquid and two solid fits, reviewed privately only. None is bound to the neutral atomic gas owner. Condensed integration requires applicable phase/state binding and source review. Applied sample pressure, isotope proportions and coefficient uncertainty/covariance remain UNKNOWN. Molecular spin-isomer populations do not apply to a monatomic species. No B2/B12 motif properties, equilibrium fractions, latent heats, boiling point, phase diagram or arbitrary-pressure response are inferred.

## Implemented outputs and validation

The [reader chapter](../../records/0005-Boron-B/0005-Boron-B-Thermochemistry.md), [structured evaluation](../../records/0005-Boron-B/data/structured/0005-Boron-B-NIST-Thermochemistry.yaml), [readable table](../../records/0005-Boron-B/tables/0005-Boron-B-TABLE-010-Thermodynamic-Functions.md), [CSV](../../records/0005-Boron-B/tables/0005-Boron-B-TABLE-010-Thermodynamic-Functions.csv) and [SVG chart](../../records/0005-Boron-B/graphs/0005-Boron-B-GRAPH-011-Heat-Capacity.svg) share the same retained source, state, units, range and explicit unknown context. The existing curated GAS-only importer, append guards, slot checks, numerical validation and native plot generator are reused; no production-code or schema change is needed. Native preview received actual visual inspection. This supplemental chart earns zero standalone A/B panel credit.

The [batch receipt](../../data/quality/thermal-boron-batch-2026-10-06.json) records exact changed files, source/artifact hashes, preservation, executed tests, terminal results, migrations and repository state. Source-transcription and arithmetic checks are not independent calorimetry or experimental replication. Global totals are 40 thermal owners / 139 fits / 14,039 rows / 71 bounded thermal source gaps and 268 supplemental elemental charts. All 119 canonical identities remain represented. All 143 master tasks, 4,248 confirmed-domain reviews and 2,587 standalone confirmed-element panels remain pending; zero elements are certified fully advanced. The [existing selector](../../data/research/mat-update-review.json) and [MAT TODO](../../data/quality/MAT-TODO.json) retain those boundaries.

## Next executable requirement

Audit authored Carbon 0006 and its applicable primary thermochemical sources. Neutral MAT:0006:ATOM:C is at /states/0; preserve diamond, graphite, graphene, nanotube, fullerene and other species/state contexts. Accept atomic gas only under an applicable canonical subject binding, or review explicit condensed phase/state bindings first. Graph slots 001–012 are reserved, including graph 012 without a physical chart; graph 013 is first free. Ten physical tables occupy 001–010 and no table manifest exists: reconcile those existing IDs/files additively before adding table 011. Reviewed candidates are asset_slots {table:11,graph:13}; repeat physical and manifest collision checks immediately before generation. No equivalent Carbon WebBook work was found; SRC-000085 is distinct CODATA graphite standard-state/formation data. Recompute the next unreserved source ID after this Boron accession and repeat work deduplication. Preserve the master and authored bytes, then continue 0007–0012 individually. Universal atomic-child projection, 71 bounded thermal source gaps, transport/dynamics/domain acceptance, source metadata/documentation and remaining standalone images stay pending. Source/state/table/chart acceptance precedes illustrations; MAT remains PARTIAL.

sources.scope_note: A species-specific gas retrieval of the existing Boron WebBook work SRC-000064; original electron-affinity/ion-energetics metadata remains byte-identical. Same-work linkage is not independent corroboration.
sources.scope: The exact publisher species is B with InChI=1S/B, not B2, B ions or an equilibrium vapor mixture. One mole of the source species is one mole of B atoms. No molecular factor of two applies. The gas-only response supplies one fit for 4137.895–6000 K. A separate retained condensed-phase diagnostic contains one LIQUID fit and two SOLID fits. Those fits are not imported, relabelled, or bound to the neutral atomic GAS state. No gas evaluation below the source minimum 4137.895 K is justified. The retained source limits do not themselves establish a boiling point, a gas stability boundary or a pressure-dependent phase boundary. Existing B-10/B-11 isotope records and atomic-weight data retain separate scope. No isotope-specific gas properties or numeric isotope abundances are inferred from this elemental fit or its listed molecular weight. The Shomate equations contain no pressure variable. Applied pressure, arbitrary-pressure EOS and phase diagrams are not inferred. Separate source entropy reference-pressure labels belong to those original data only. No B/B2 equilibrium fraction, dimer dissociation, ionisation fraction, charge-state mixture or molecular nuclear-spin population is calculated or assigned. Fit boundaries from separate phases and enthalpy reference offsets are retained as reported and are not a constructed phase-transition path or latent-heat calculation. Coefficient uncertainty and covariance are unreported. Printed-temperature cells, output rounding and numerical derivative residuals are source-format/software checks, not physical uncertainty. Independent transcription arithmetic against publisher values and positive samples within the fit do not establish experimental replication, new calorimetry, complete Boron thermophysics or element completion.
sources.reference: Chase, M.W., Jr. (1998), NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables, Fourth Edition. Fit comment: Data last reviewed in June, 1983.
